title: I've been building AutoSprite for almost a year now. One character image can now become a full 8-direction isometric spritesheet for cozy games
author: beelllllll
selftext:
Hey everyone! Back with another AutoSprite update. I've been working on this almost every day for close to a year now, and it's been pretty crazy seeing how far it's come.

I originally started building this because I always wanted an easier way to make characters for my own games. The idea was simple: take one character image, turn it into animations, and actually be able to play with it instead of spending hours putting spritesheets together.

Lately I've been really focused on isometric and 2.5D cozy games. Getting a character to look consistent while walking, farming, and dancing in 8 different directions is surprisingly difficult.

Some of the things I've added and improved recently:

* **8-direction isometric spritesheets** for farming sims, life sims, and cozy games
* Better character consistency across different animations and directions
* Idle, walk, run, farming, dancing, and custom animations
* Equipment and character customization workflows
* A playable browser preview so you can actually test your character
* MCP integration with Claude Code and Codex to help build games with your generated assets

My goal is still the same: one character image in, a complete playable character out.

It's definitely not perfect yet. Getting animations to loop smoothly, keeping equipment consistent, and making farming actions look good from every angle are all things I'm still working on.

But I feel like we're getting closer to making it possible for anyone with a cozy game idea to actually bring their characters to life.

You can try it here: [https://autosprite.io](https://autosprite.io)

I'd love to hear what you guys think, especially anyone working on an isometric cozy game. What's the biggest pain point you still have with character animations?

Thanks everyone for all the feedback over the past year. It's genuinely helped me figure out what to build next!

comments.author: PurchaseCommercial34
comments.body: the thing that usually bites with 8-dir sheets is the feet. if the ground contact point isn't on the same pixel in every direction and every frame, the character looks like it's sliding when it turns on an iso grid, even when each animation looks fine on its own. do you normalize a ground anchor per frame, or leave that to whoever imports the sheet? also curious whether you generate all 8 directions or do 5 and mirror. mirroring is cheap but it breaks as soon as the character holds a tool in one hand, which for farming is pretty much always

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: It uses all 8 directions and we do a lot of post-processing behind the scenes to get it as close as polished as possible. These are great questions !

replies.author: beelllllll
replies.body: This is in the browser as a 3js project. It’s gotten really powerful! I find that agents work much better and faster in browser code vs unity or godot.

replies.author: ManduLaboratory
replies.body: Wow... that tilt shift blur is insanly detailed. great job.

comments.author: _Fauxpaw
comments.body: I've noticed a lot of annoying inconsistencies between different animation sets. I imagine a big problem is creating consistency between when you create your first set of animations, and then followup sets of animations.. the sprite of the girl randomly grows and shrinks in size, the band around her straw hat changes in colour, et cetera.
